title: M1 Public Broadcaster Resumes News After 44-Day Blackout, but Editorial Independence Questioned
detail: Hungary's public broadcaster M1 resumed news broadcasts on August 20 — the national holiday — 44 days after PM Péter Magyar's government suspended them on July 7 to rebuild the station as 'independent and credible' following years of pro-Fidesz propaganda under the old MTVA leadership. The new flagship bulletin, Híradó, launched with presenter Máté Kis and, according to independent outlet Telex, included opposition and critical voices for the first time in years. Two respected journalists purged during the Orbán era — Antónia Mészáros (removed from public media after a 2010 interview with then-PM Orbán) and Ádám Bősze — returned for a one-day celebratory broadcast. But the relaunch itself drew press-freedom criticism: interim managers' August 4 appointment of an editor-in-chief and presenter for the new news desk was reversed within 24 hours after Magyar commented 'I don't think so…' on a Facebook post flagging the appointees' prior ties to Fidesz-era figures — a direct PM intervention in an outlet whose independence had just been proclaimed. Former Fidesz MP János Pócs accused Magyar of building 'a dictatorship.'

media.caption: Máté Kis presents Híradó, M1's relaunched flagship news bulletin
